topic.title: company name, never the job
topic.claim: Your parents tell relatives your company's name, never your job.
topic.moment: A relative asks what you do and papa jumps in with the company's name, and the title just never comes up.

turn.believed: They skip your job title because they don't understand what you actually do.
turn.actually: They lead with the company because the brand lands instantly, while your real work can't be bragged in one word.

topic.because: A famous company name does the status-work in one breath; nobody needs it explained. Your actual role is complicated, foreign, hard to make a relative go 'wah'. So they trade the truth of your job for the shine of your employer.
topic.payoff: They don't name your job because it can't be bragged in one word. The company can. So that's the part they keep.
topic.feeling: the gentle comedy of being reduced to a logo you're proud of anyway
topic.villain: the arrangement where a career only counts if it fits in a brand name
topic.behaviour: parents introduce their kids by employer, never by actual role
topic.mechanism: a known company name carries status instantly while your real job can't, so they keep the part relatives understand
topic.group: adults with jobs their parents can't quite explain
topic.send_to: a friend whose parents brag about their company but can't say their role
topic.why_now: wedding-season introductions where the 'what does your child do' question flies
